requirement:
An OpenAI configuration MAY omit `model`; the effective model MUST then be
`gpt-6.1-sol`. When `options.reasoning.effort` is omitted, the request MUST use
`low` effort, preserving other reasoning options. When `options.max_output_tokens`
is omitted, the request MUST use an output-token limit of 16,384. These option
defaults MUST apply even when the model is overridden. An explicit model,
reasoning effort, or output-token limit MUST override its corresponding default.
Defaults MUST NOT be written into omitted configuration fields on serialization.
An explicitly empty model MUST still be rejected.
rationale:
`requirements.authoring.openai_defaults` is satisfied. The permission to omit `model` adds no separate obligation. The mandatory obligations and their evidence are:

| Obligation | Implementation | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| An omitted model has effective value `gpt-6.1-sol`. | `src/config.rs#impl[OpenAiConfig]/fn[model]` uses that fallback only for `None`. | `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_defaults_are_effective_only_and_explicit_values_win]` checks the effective model; `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_key_only_profile_sends_sol_low_and_accepts_overrides]` asserts the outgoing request model. |
| Omitted reasoning effort becomes `low`. | `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[options_json]` inserts the reasoning map and its missing effort entry. | Both tests above assert `low` when omitted, including in actual requests. |
| Other reasoning options are preserved. | `options_json` converts the saved options to JSON and inserts only missing entries. | The configuration test supplies `summary = 'auto'` and asserts it remains present alongside default effort. |
| An omitted output-token limit becomes 16,384. | `options_json` inserts `max_output_tokens` only if missing. | Both tests assert 16,384. |
| Default effort applies with an overridden model. | The OpenAI branch in `options_json` does not depend on the model value. | Both tests cover `gpt-6-luna` with omitted effort and assert `low`. |
| Default output-token limit applies with an overridden model. | The same model-independent branch inserts the limit. | Both tests cover `gpt-6-luna` and assert 16,384 when the limit is omitted. |
| An explicit model overrides its default. | `OpenAiConfig::model` returns the stored `Some` value. | Both tests assert the overridden model; the configuration test also covers explicitly selecting the default model. |
| Explicit reasoning effort overrides its default. | `options_json` uses entry insertion rather than replacement. | The configuration test asserts `medium` and `high`; the CLI test asserts outgoing `medium`. |
| An explicit output-token limit overrides its default. | `options_json` likewise retains an existing limit. | The CLI test supplies 8192 and asserts that request value. |
| Serialization does not populate an omitted model. | `src/config.rs#struct[OpenAiConfig]`, reachable through the marked methods' receiver types, stores an optional model and skips serialization of `None`. The effective-model accessor does not mutate it. | The configuration test asserts serialized model presence exactly matches explicit input and checks round-trip equality. |
| Serialization does not populate omitted reasoning effort. | `options_json` defaults a separate JSON value, leaving the saved options map unchanged. | The configuration test calls `options_json`, then asserts serialized effort presence exactly matches input and checks round-trip equality. |
| Serialization does not populate an omitted output-token limit. | The same separate JSON conversion leaves the saved map unchanged. | The configuration test asserts serialized output lacks `max_output_tokens` after effective defaults have been obtained. |
| An explicitly empty model is rejected. | `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` checks the effective model for emptiness, through `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[model_ref]`; an explicit empty string does not take the fallback. | The configuration test asserts parsing `model = ''` fails. |

All listed tests carry the subject's `{test}` reference. The implementation is reachable from its marked roots, including the configuration types governing serialization. The additional validation in the marked roots is covered by their other implementation references: `requirements.authoring.configuration_storage` specifies option pass-through and reserved-field protection, and `requirements.configuration.loading` specifies reporting invalid feature settings. No unacknowledged gap was found.

text: :::{req} openai_defaults
An OpenAI configuration MAY omit `model`; the effective model MUST then be
`gpt-6.1-sol`. When `options.reasoning.effort` is omitted, the request MUST use
`low` effort, preserving other reasoning options. When `options.max_output_tokens`
is omitted, the request MUST use an output-token limit of 16,384. These option
defaults MUST apply even when the model is overridden. An explicit model,
reasoning effort, or output-token limit MUST override its corresponding default.
Defaults MUST NOT be written into omitted configuration fields on serialization.
An explicitly empty model MUST still be rejected.
:::{req} configuration_storage
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.
Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
:::{req} loading
An operation MUST load user configuration only when its requirements call for
user settings. A missing user file MUST represent absent user configuration;
whether the operation can proceed MUST be defined by the feature. Loading MUST
NOT create a file, repair malformed input, or supply an undocumented selection.
When loading configuration, Habeas MUST report unreadable files, invalid TOML,
unsupported user-file versions, unknown common keys, and invalid common field
types. It MUST validate the feature sections used by that operation and report
invalid feature settings with the file and setting identified. Unknown keys in
an explicitly documented provider-owned options map MUST follow that feature's
validation rules.
An operation MUST NOT require or semantically validate configuration for a
feature it does not use. This isolation MUST NOT suppress TOML syntax errors in
a shared file that the operation otherwise needs to parse. In particular,
ordinary validation still requires a parseable `book.toml` while remaining
independent of authoring settings and the user configuration file. It MUST apply
the selected workspace's evidence path policy without loading its model clients
or credentials.
:::{req} feature_sections
Each configurable feature MUST define the name and typed data structure of its
user section and any supported project section, citing these common configuration
requirements. The feature MUST specify its supported keys, value types, defaults,
validation rules, and the precedence or combination rules for user settings,
project settings, and invocation options. It MUST specify the behavior of an
absent section and which operations require that section.
Feature-specific fields MUST stay within the feature's section. A feature MUST
NOT reinterpret another feature's settings or change the shared file locations
or schema version. A feature MAY define a provider-owned options map, but MUST
document that boundary and how those options are validated.
